title: Meet Jonathan Hock, LCSW
content:
Jonathan Hock is a Houston-based psychotherapist, US Army veteran, and a pragmatic philosopher. He chiefly operates from an existential and phenomenological perspective, though his philosophical style is a challenge to pinpoint exactly. Most of his clients are men and he guides them in the art of self-examination, assisting them to discern and identify their values, and to actualize a felt-sense of a well lived life. He is a Licensed Clinical Social Worker in the State of Texas and a graduate of both The University of Houston and Suffolk University (Boston, MA). 

Jonathan's values of grit and steadfastness were forged in his early blue-collar experiences as a combat-arms veteran, cell-tower climber, and welder. He completed a two-year post-graduate clinical social work fellowship at the Texas A&M Department of Psychiatry. He is currently in a long-term training at the Center for Existential Analysis and Logotherapy (CEAL) towards his diplomate status as an Existential Analyst.

Jonathan maintains a healthy, Heideggerian distrust of technology and much prefers the company of physical books and in-person dialogue. Much of his spare time is spent reading on the topics of philosophy, history, religion, anthropology, and mythology. His love for nonfiction and human culture inevitably seeps its way into his therapeutic practice. He enjoys strength and flexibility training and often craves communion with nature. He lives with his husband and senior cat in a modest townhome in Montrose and sees clients in his home office.
